title: Does a Tiny Fine-Tune Make Open Models Better at Controlling (Hiding) Their CoT?

original_idea.body: LoRA fine-tune to hide a CoT feature; measure sample-efficiency and monitorability side-effects.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: tests robustness of the 'low controllability is safe' assumption against the cheapest adversary (LoRA).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: LoRA fine-tuning + monitorability eval needs solid ML fundamentals beyond pure inference.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused; LoRA training + sample-efficiency curve is a contained but multi-step pipeline.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected medium-horizon threat (cheap adversary breaking a safety property) labs under-prioritize; needs no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: LoRA on a 7B model fits a single consumer GPU but is more than pure inference.

novelty.reasoning: METR showed it narrowly; sample-efficiency on open models plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Tiny-finetune CoT-controllability on open models plausibly open.
